{{Short description|Application of epistemology in specific fields}}
{{Epistemology sidebar}}
{{Philosophy sidebar}}
'''Applied epistemology''' refers to the study that determines whether the systems of investigation that seek the truth lead to true beliefs about the world.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|last=Laudan|first=Larry|title=Truth, Error, and Criminal Law: An Essay in Legal Epistemology|publisher=Cambridge University Press|year=2006|isbn=978-1-139-45708-8|location=Cambridge, MA|pages=2|language=en}}</ref> A specific conceptualization cites that it attempts to reveal whether these systems contribute to [[Epistemology|epistemic]] aims.<ref name=":6">{{Cite journal|last=Gorichanaz|first=Tim|date=December 2017|title=Applied epistemology and understanding in information studies|url=http://informationr.net/ir/22-4/paper776.html|journal=Information Research|volume=22|issue=4 }}</ref> It is applied in practices outside of [[philosophy]] like [[science]] and [[mathematics]].<ref name=":0" />

Once applied epistemology is described as a method in an epistemological search, it implies that the [[methodology]] is supported by an epistemological foundation.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Gordon|first=Susan|title=Neurophenomenology and Its Applications to Psychology|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|year=2013|isbn=978-1-4614-7238-4|location=New York|pages=34}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last1=Mustapha|first1=Zakari|title=Contractor Health and Safety Compliance for Small to Medium-Sized Construction Companies|last2=Aigbavboa|first2=Clinton|last3=Thwala|first3=Wellington|publisher=CRC Press|year=2018|isbn=978-1-138-08155-0|location=Boca Raton, FL|pages=115|language=en}}</ref>

== Background ==
Applied epistemology forms part of the concept of "[[applied philosophy]]" as theorists begin to distinguish it from "[[applied ethics]]".<ref name=":1">{{Cite book|last1=Lippert-Rasmussen|first1=Kasper|title=A Companion to Applied Philosophy|last2=Brownlee|first2=Kimberley|last3=Coady|first3=David|publisher=John Wiley & Sons|year=2016|isbn=978-1-118-86913-0|location=Chichester, West Sussex|pages=16, 19|language=en}}</ref> It is argued that "applied philosophy" is a broader field, and that it has parts that are not subdisciplines of applied ethics.<ref name=":1" /> The emergence of "applied philosophy" gained traction after it was proposed that philosophy can be applied to contemporary issues.<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal|last=Battersby|first=Mark E.|date=1989|title=Critical Thinking as Applied Epistemology: Relocating Critical Thinking in the Philosophical Landscape|journal=Informal Logic|volume=XI|citeseerx=10.1.1.894.5514}}</ref>

Applied epistemology emerged from epistemologists routine examinations that determine whether truth-seeking practices like science and mathematics are capable of delivering truths.<ref name=":0" /> It draws from epistemological theorizing to address pressing epistemic matters of practical value.<ref name=":2" /> An epistemological question assumes a philosophical form once it deals with the type of knowledge or justification that is presupposed in most ordinary contexts.<ref name=":5" />

In its infancy, applied epistemology had been equated with social epistemology.<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Lippert-Rasmussen|first1=Kasper|title=A Companion to Applied Philosophy|last2=Brownlee|first2=Kimberley|last3=Coady|first3=David|publisher=John Wiley & Sons|year=2017|isbn=978-1-118-86913-0|location=Malden, MA|pages=54}}</ref> Later theorizing established that, while there are overlapping aspects, not all social epistemology is applied and not all applied epistemology is social.<ref name=":4">{{Cite book|last1=Coady|first1=David|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=wQtpDwAAQBAJ&dq=%22applied+epistemology%22+%22social+epistemology%22&pg=PT27|title=The Routledge Handbook of Applied Epistemology|last2=Chase|first2=James|date=2018-09-03|publisher=Routledge|isbn=978-1-317-39314-6|language=en}}</ref> A proposed analogy to distinguish applied epistemology from epistemology holds that it involves the general opposition between theory and application.<ref name=":10">{{Cite book|last=Carvallo|first=M. E.|title=Nature, Cognition and System I: Current Systems-Scientific Research on Natural and Cognitive Systems|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|year=2012|isbn=978-94-010-7844-3|location=Dordrecht|pages=68}}</ref> In applied epistemology, theories in epistemology are applied for solving practical problems. The theoretical constructions in this environment can be modified or reorganized in function of the primary target.<ref name=":10" />

== Concept ==
[[File:epistemology.png|left|thumb|The relationship between basic concepts of epistemology|300x300px]]
[[File:David Hume.jpg|thumb|While applied epistemology is considered a new term, it has been used in the past. [[David Hume]] used the concept in his argument against belief in miracles.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Coady|first=David|title=What to Believe Now: Applying Epistemology to Contemporary Issues|publisher=John Wiley & Sons|year=2012|isbn=978-1-4051-9993-3|location=Malden, MA|pages=3}}</ref>]]
Applied epistemology is informed by skepticism in philosophy, as it maintains that things should not be taken at face value – that, in reflection, what people knew as "truths" could turn out to be false.<ref name=":5">{{Cite book|last=Fumerton|first=Richard|title=Epistemology|publisher=John Wiley & Sons|year=2009|isbn=978-1-4051-2566-6|location=Malden, MA|language=en}}</ref> Applied epistemology has been concerned with practical questions about truth, knowledge, and other epistemic values but these are not all social questions.<ref name=":4" /> It asks questions about what we know and are justified in believing.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Fumerton|first=Richard|title=Epistemology and Science: Some Metaphilosophical Reflections|journal=Philosophical Topics|volume=45|issue=1|pages=1–16|doi=10.5840/philtopics20174511|s2cid=171850411}}</ref>

Applied epistomology is also considered one of the three branches of epistemology along with [[normative epistemology]] and [[metaepistemology]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|last=Kyriacou|first=Christos|title=Metaepistemology|url=https://iep.utm.edu/meta-epi/|url-status=live|access-date=2021-06-09|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160501172421/http://www.iep.utm.edu:80/meta-epi/ |archive-date=2016-05-01 }}</ref> The normative branch is concerned with first-order theorizing about the formation of justified beliefs, knowledge, and truths.<ref name=":2" /> Metaepistemology, on the other hand, deals with higher order epistemological questions, particularly, the fundamental aspects of epistemic theorizing.<ref name=":2" /> According to philosopher [[Richard Fumerton]], metaepistemology is concerned with questions about what knowledge – including justification, rationality, and evidence – is.<ref name=":5" /> A conceptualization cites that the applied epistemologist operates within a background of naturalist metaepistemology and reliabilist first-order epistemology.<ref name=":7">{{Cite book|last=Michaelian|first=Kourken|title=Mental Time Travel: Episodic Memory and Our Knowledge of the Personal Past|publisher=MIT Press|year=2016|isbn=978-0-262-03409-8|location=Cambridge, MA|pages=38}}</ref>

The following table demonstrates the place of applied epistemology in relation to epistemology and to the parallels between ethics and epistemology covering a specific topic according to Mark Battersby.<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Battersby|first1=Mark|title=Inquiry: A New Paradigm for Critical Thinking|last2=Bailin|first2=Sharon|publisher=University of Windsor|year=2018|isbn=978-0-920233-84-9|pages=255|language=en}}</ref> Other philosophers have different conceptions of the relationships.<ref name=":2" />

The main domains of applied epistemology include [[education]] and [[pedagogy]], [[therapy]], [[politics]], [[STEM fields|science and technology]], [[The arts|arts]], and [[artificial intelligence]].<ref name=":10" />

== Applications ==

As part of "applied philosophy", applied epistemology has been applied to different contemporary practices and issues. This include its application to [[critical thinking]] or informal logic, information systems, and pressing social concerns. In the area of critical thinking, there is the underlying idea that thinking clearly and carefully about any issue needs the understanding and application of fundamental epistemological concepts.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Goldman |first1=Alvin |title=Social Epistemology: Essential Readings |last2=Whitcomb |first2=Dennis |publisher=Oxford University Press |year=2011 |isbn=978-0-19-533461-6 |location=Oxford |pages=138 |language=en}}</ref> Theorists draw from philosophical theories to address real-life epistemic issues.

=== Communication ===
According to V.D. Singh, since [[general semantics]] is a general theory of evaluation – that it considers the interrelations among events that transpire within ourselves and the world around us as well as how he obtain information or talk about such events and how we behave – makes it an up-to-date and scientifically based applied epistemology.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Geetha|first=Bhasker|date=2013|title=General Semantics and Effective Communication|journal=ETC: A Review of General Semantics|volume=70|issue=2|pages=123–129}}</ref> Scholars cite the case of fake news as an issue that can be addressed by applied epistemology. It is posited that corrupted or fake information can be unmasked through an epistemological investigation that answers three questions: 1. What is fake news?; 2. What are the mechanisms that foster the production and spread of fake news; and, 3. which interventions can address it?<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Bernecker|first1=Sven|title=The Epistemology of Fake News|last2=Flowerree|first2=Amy K.|last3=Grundmann|first3=Thomas|publisher=Oxford University Press|year=2021|isbn=978-0-19-886397-7|location=Oxford, UK|pages=6}}</ref>

=== Scientific research ===
Applied epistemology in science has been described as the specific mental frameworks utilized by scientists in their research and activities that are considered processes of acquiring [[knowledge]].<ref name=":13">{{Cite book|last1=Markham|first1=Ian S.|title=The Companion to Said Nursi Studies|last2=Sayilgan|first2=Zeyneb|publisher=Wipf and Stock Publishers|year=2017|isbn=978-1-4982-9222-1|location=Eugene, OR|pages=245|language=en}}</ref> These frameworks also serve as the ground of the sociology of science.<ref name=":13" /> There is also the case of the philosophy of science, which provides epistemic justifications for scientific reasoning and choice.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Mladenović|first=Bojana|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7-UvDwAAQBAJ&dq=%22applied+epistemology%22+%22sociology+of+science%22&pg=PT20|title=Kuhn's Legacy: Epistemology, Metaphilosophy, and Pragmatism|date=2017-09-05|publisher=Columbia University Press|isbn=978-0-231-52074-4|language=en}}</ref> It is considered an applied epistemology due to the characterization that it is precise, formal, and normative.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Mladenović|first=Bojana|title=Kuhn's Legacy: Epistemology, Metaphilosophy, and Pragmatism|publisher=Columbia University Press|year=2017|isbn=978-0-231-52074-4|location=New York|language=en}}</ref>

An example of the deployment of applied epistemology in scientific research is the Toolbox Project. It is an initiative that apply philosophical analysis to enhance collaborative, cross-disciplinary scientific research by improving cross-disciplinary communication.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=O'Rourke|first=Michael|date=2013|title=Philosophical Intervention and Cross-Disciplinary Science: the Story of the Toolbox Project|journal=Synthese|volume=190|issue=11|pages=1937–1954|doi=10.1007/s11229-012-0175-y|s2cid=5081752}}</ref> There are also scholars who consider the application of epistemologically relevant psychology to science as applied epistemology.<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Gholson|first1=Barry|title=Psychology of Science: Contributions to Metascience|last2=Shadish (jr.)|first2=William R.|last3=Neimeyer|first3=Robert|last4=Houts|first4=Arthur|publisher=Cambridge University Press|year=1989|isbn=0-521-35410-2|location=Cambridge, UK|language=en}}</ref> Aside from its role in scientific and technological advancement, the concept is also applied in the areas of ethics and policy.<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Cameron|first1=Nigel|title=Nanoscale: Issues and Perspectives for the Nano Century|last2=Mitchell|first2=M. Ellen|publisher=John Wiley & Sons|year=2007|isbn=978-0-470-08419-9|location=Hoboken, NJ|pages=147|language=en}}</ref> It is argued that the instincts that guide actual scientific practice are yet to be fully recognized, scrutinized, and justified.<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Allhoff|first1=Fritz|title=Nanoethics: The Ethical and Social Implications of Nanotechnology|last2=Lin|first2=Patrick|last3=Moor|first3=James H.|last4=Weckert|first4=John|publisher=John Wiley & Sons|year=2007|isbn=978-0-470-08416-8|location=Hoboken, NJ|pages=113|language=en}}</ref>

=== Informal logic ===
According to Mark Battersby, the method of critical thinking or informal logic can be considered a form of applied epistemology.<ref name=":3" /> This method involves the assessment of the strength of evidences that afford conclusions can only be made if the domain within which the argument is presented is taken into account.<ref name=":8">{{Cite book|last1=Walton|first1=Douglas|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ujaoDQAAQBAJ&dq=applied+epistemology+informal+logic&pg=PT237|title=Historical Foundations of Informal Logic|last2=Brinton|first2=Alan|date=2016-12-05|publisher=Routledge|isbn=978-1-351-93070-3|language=en}}</ref> For Battersby, this constitutes applied epistemology, since it is about grounding assessments of arguments as they occur within them.<ref name=":8" /> Mark Weinstein maintained that a focus on the account of how acceptability is transmitted from premises to conclusion show close theoretical parallel between informal logic and applied epistemology.<ref name=":8" /> It is argued that rather than rules of logic, epistemological norms constitute the philosophical core of informal logic and that there is a close parallel between informal logic and applied ethics.<ref name=":11" /> Based on these factors, scholars such as Battersby and Weinstein maintain that informal logic should be classified as applied epistemology instead of logic.<ref name=":11">{{Cite book|last1=Eemeren|first1=Frans H. van|title=Fundamentals of Argumentation Theory: A Handbook of Historical Backgrounds and Contemporary Developments|last2=Grootendorst|first2=Rob|last3=Johnson|first3=Ralph H.|last4=Plantin|first4=Christian|last5=Willard|first5=Charles A.|publisher=Routledge|year=2013|isbn=978-1-136-68804-1|pages=183|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":8" />

=== Social issues ===
It has been suggested by scholars such as [[Jennifer Lackey]] that applied epistemology provides the tools in contemporary epistemology's evaluation of the issues of social concern.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Lackey|first=Jennifer|title=Applied Epistemology|publisher=Oxford University Press|year=2021|isbn=978-0-19-883365-9|location=Oxford, UK|pages=3|language=en}}</ref> It is relevant to issues affecting social groups since it helps in answering the recurring practical question, "what to believe now".<ref>{{Cite book |last=Moshman |first=David |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=EBOLBQAAQBAJ&dq=%22applied+epistemology%22+social+issues&pg=PA124 |title=Epistemic Cognition and Development: The Psychology of Justification and Truth |publisher=Psychology Press |year=2015 |isbn=978-1-84872-513-3 |location=New York, NY |pages=124 |language=en}}</ref> Applied epistemology is also considered capable of unmasking the contribution of the features of public deliberation to a group's reliability and provide a basis for a [[Reliabilism|reliabilist]] rationale for democracy in the process.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Goldman|first=Alvin I.|title=Reliabilism and Contemporary Epistemology: Essays|publisher=Oxford University Press, USA|year=2012|isbn=978-0-19-981287-5|location=New York|pages=273|language=en}}</ref> Applied epistemology has also been employed in examining feminism, particularly with respect to the evaluation of the agency of women and what is the relevance of giving it authorial primacy within studies of knowledge.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Coady |first1=David |title=The Routledge Handbook of Applied Epistemology |last2=Chase |first2=James |publisher=Routledge |year=2018 |isbn=978-1-317-39314-6 |language=en}}</ref>

=== Information studies ===
According to Tim Gorichanaz, applied epistemology allows information studies to benefit from the field of philosophy particularly since it rarely focuses on the evaluation of epistemic concepts.<ref name=":6" /> It is also suggested that applying the concept to information system can bridge the information processing models of cognition and constructivist perspectives on knowledge.<ref name=":14">{{Cite book|last=Hoshmand|first=Lisa Tsoi|title=Orientation to Inquiry in a Reflective Professional Psychology|publisher=State University of New York Press|year=1994|isbn=0-7914-2115-5|location=Albany, NY|pages=133|language=en}}</ref> Applied epistemology can be prominent in the "schema" or the cognitive organization of meaningful information.<ref name=":14" /> Specifically, it is the information structure that can be modified to represent knowledge of interrelationships between events, objects, and situations that we encounter.<ref name=":14" />

=== Psychology ===
Applied epistemology is relevant to the field of psychology and cognitive science as it focuses on the study of particular epistemic problems and processes and is characterized as part of an empirical field.<ref name=":7" /> It addresses how cognitive agents go about constructing epistemically adequate representations of the world.<ref name=":7" /> The content of the psychological experts or therapists' cognitive organization or "knowing" processes has also been described as applied epistemology. This system of knowing allows a better understanding of a patient's problems.<ref name=":9">{{Cite book|last1=Caro|first1=Isabel|title=General Semantics in Psychotherapy: Selected Writings on Methods Aiding Therapy|last2=Read|first2=Charlotte Schuchardt|publisher=Institute of GS|year=2002|isbn=0-910780-16-1|location=New York, NY|pages=327|language=en}}</ref> It also represents part of the knowledge system in which interventions that facilitate change can be drawn.<ref name=":9" />

=== Law ===
Legal epistemology is considered a form of applied epistemology for its evaluation of whether legal systems of investigation that seeks the truth are structured in a manner that actually lead to justified and true beliefs.<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Bergsmo|first1=Morten|title=Philosophical Foundations of International Criminal Law: Foundational Concepts|last2=Buis|first2=Emiliano J.|publisher=Torkel Opsahl Academic EPublisher|year=2019|isbn=978-82-8348-119-8|location=Brussel|pages=288}}</ref> Applied epistemics allows the legal system to draw from philosophy. For instance, [[David Hume]] stated that, "we entertain a suspicion concerning any matter of fact, when the witnesses contradict each other; when they are but few, or a doubtful character; when they have an interest in what they affirm; when they deliver their testimony with hesitation, or on the contrary, with too violent asseverations."  This generic view is said to allow legal procedure the effective evaluation of testimonies.<ref name=":4" />

=== Philosophy ===
Applied epistemology is also used in evaluating philosophical issues. This is the case when empirical perspective is applied to test philosophical theories.<ref name=":12">{{Cite book|last1=Shimony|first1=A.|title=Naturalistic Epistemology: A Symposium of Two Decades|last2=Nails|first2=Debra|publisher=D. Reidel Publishing Company|year=1987|isbn=978-94-010-8168-9|location=Dordrecht|pages=210|language=en}}</ref> While this approach does not eliminate analytic and conceptual issues, it can make them clearer.<ref name=":12" /> It also increases the probability of theorists to examine evidences that tend to be overlooked.<ref name=":12" />

=== Cybernetics ===
Applied epistemology is also significant in [[cybernetics]], which involves the control and communication of living and man-made systems.<ref name=":15" /> Modern cybernetics, particularly, is considered an applied epistemology for its focus on how the process of the construction of models of the systems is influenced by the living and man-made systems in its goal of understanding the similarities and differences of the inner workings of the organic and machine processes.<ref name=":15">{{Cite book|last=|title=Blackie's Dictionary of Computer Science|date=2013|publisher=S. Chand Publishing|isbn=978-81-219-4153-2|location=New Delhi|pages=42|language=en}}</ref> Once applied to cybernetics, applied epistemology also contributes in shaping responses to global and local issues since it helps construct a type of political epistemology that can lead to a holistic and socially responsible discourse and practice.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Espejo|first=Raul|date=July 2015|title=The Cybernetics of Self-organisation|journal=Kybernetes|volume=42|issue=6/7|doi=10.1108/K-08-2015-0198}}</ref>
